purpose: Persist source findings used to verify Norderhov old rectory's coordinate, building chronology, 1716 association, museum reuse and separation from neighbouring components.

legacyCoordinate.assessment: Unsupported point approximately 863.3 metres west-north-west of the rectory.

historic timber rectory beside Norderhov church

chronology.event: The ground floor of the south wing, later called Svenskestua, was built.
The rectory became associated with the Battle of Norderhov and the memory of Anna Colbjørnsdatter's aid to Norwegian forces.
chronology.certainty: documented event with later memory tradition

chronology.event: A second floor was added to the south wing.
The building received a new roof.
Peter Christen Asbjørnsen and Jørgen Moe first met at the rectory.
The rectory ceased serving as the parish priest's private residence and Ringerikes Museum moved into the building.

interpretationLimits: The canonical point represents the historic rectory main building now used by Ringerikes Museum.
Year 1716 is an event and memory anchor, not the construction year of the whole building.
The exact details of Anna Colbjørnsdatter's actions should be presented with source-critical room rather than as an uncontested script.
Norderhov church is a separate medieval church and active cemetery environment.
Munkestua and the wider rectory farm are separate components.
The existing desc and popupDesc remain unchanged under place-description governance.
